payload.explanation: Hypothermic newborn lambs need gradual warming — rapid heat causes shock. Colostrum within six hours is critical for immune function. A vet call prioritises correctly given the weakness.

payload.snippet: During a farm fire drill exercise the instructor mentioned casually that a real fire in a hay barn propagates to full involvement in under ninety seconds and the only safe course was immediate evacuation, never attempting to move stock.
options: understand and remember this fact so that in any real incident he would prioritise personal evacuation and raise the alarm rather than attempting to free animals
feel confident he could move several animals in ninety seconds since he was quick
memorise the locations of all the animal release mechanisms in case he could help in a real fire
ask the instructor what equipment would be needed to save the animals in that time
payload.explanation: Hay barn fires reach full intensity in under ninety seconds — attempting to free animals has killed more people than the fires themselves. This rule must be internalised, not planned around.

payload.snippet: She was working on a remote hill farm when she noticed that the quad bike she was about to use had a slow puncture in one rear tyre, and the track to the farthest fields included steep descents.
options: report the puncture to the farmer and refuse to take the vehicle on steep terrain until it was repaired
inflate the tyre manually and check it again at the top of each hill
drive carefully and use the brakes heavily on descents to compensate
use the bike for the flat sections only and walk the steep descents
payload.explanation: A slow puncture on a rear tyre of a quad bike on steep descents is a rollover risk — farm vehicles must be in safe mechanical condition before being driven on challenging terrain.

payload.snippet: He found the farm's pesticide store unlocked and open with several containers tipped over on the floor and a strong chemical smell, and the farmer was unreachable by phone.
options: seal off the area, prevent entry by anyone, evacuate anyone nearby, and call emergency services — treat it as a chemical incident
quickly right the tipped containers and close the store before finding the farmer
open all the windows in the store to ventilate the chemical smell
call the farmer repeatedly until he answered before taking any other action
payload.explanation: An uncontrolled pesticide spill with strong fumes is a chemical incident — evacuation and emergency services are required even if the farmer is unreachable.

payload.snippet: The class was on a residential farm stay when one child from the group developed a high fever, vomiting, and severe diarrhoea twelve hours after they had all eaten the same meal prepared with farm produce.
options: isolate the child and notify the farmer and supervising teacher immediately — other group members may also be incubating the illness
assume it was unrelated to the food since no one else was sick yet
give the child paracetamol and monitor overnight before deciding
clean the kitchen thoroughly before raising the alarm to avoid panic
payload.explanation: Foodborne illness has an incubation period — other members who ate the same food may become ill within hours. Early notification allows preventive action for the whole group.

payload.snippet: She was operating a tractor under supervision when the engine stalled on a steep slope and the tractor began to roll backward even with the handbrake applied because the slope exceeded the handbrake's rated capacity.
options: immediately apply the foot brake with full force and do not release it while calling out for assistance
steer sharply to turn the tractor across the slope and use the steering to stop it
jump from the cab immediately to avoid being in the vehicle if it rolled
try to restart the engine quickly to regain drive power on the slope
payload.explanation: A rolling tractor on a steep slope must be held with foot brakes — steering alone is insufficient and jumping from a moving tractor on a slope is one of the most common causes of farm fatalities.

payload.snippet: During a school farm visit he noticed the farmer spray the edge of a crop field without putting up any exclusion signs, and the wind direction meant spray was being carried across the designated public footpath.
options: lead the group back along the footpath away from the spray area and tell the farm supervisor
hold his breath and walk the group through the spray quickly
ask the farmer loudly whether it was safe before entering the spray zone
wait upwind at the entrance to the footpath for the spraying to finish
payload.explanation: Exposure to agricultural spray on a footpath is a reportable breach of pesticide regulations — moving the group away and reporting to the farm supervisor is both the safest and legally correct response.

payload.snippet: He was on a two-week agricultural placement when the farmer told him to drive a loaded trailer down a steep track alone on his second day, without any supervised practice on slopes with load.
options: explain respectfully that he had not yet driven loaded on slopes under supervision and ask for a supervised run first
drive the trailer carefully since he had managed the unloaded tractor fine on day one
refuse the task entirely and ask to be given a different job for the rest of the placement
complete the drive very slowly and report any near misses at the end of the day
payload.explanation: Loaded trailers on steep slopes are among the highest risk farm operations — requesting supervised practice before solo work is both professional and correct.

payload.snippet: During lambing season she found a ewe that had prolapsed its uterus and was lying in distress in the far corner of the field, and the farmer was twenty minutes away by vehicle.
options: call the farmer and vet immediately and stay with the ewe without attempting to reinsert the prolapse, keeping it clean and moist if possible
attempt to gently push the prolapse back in using clean hands
leave the ewe alone since handling could make it worse and drive to get the farmer
roll the ewe onto her other side to reduce the prolapse's contact with the ground
payload.explanation: Uterine prolapse in sheep is a veterinary emergency — calling both the farmer and vet simultaneously is faster than driving, and keeping the prolapse clean without reinsertion prevents further damage.

payload.snippet: She was loading grain into a lorry with an auger when it jammed and a co-worker reached into the auger housing to clear the blockage without first isolating the power.
options: shout a warning immediately and reach for the emergency stop rather than grabbing the co-worker
grab the co-worker's arm to pull them away from the auger
shout to get away while running to find the farmer
call out to the co-worker to be careful and watch what they were doing
payload.explanation: Reaching for an emergency stop is always faster and safer than physical contact with someone near rotating machinery — grabbing the person can pull both of you into the hazard zone.

payload.snippet: The farm's slurry lagoon had developed a visible crust over two thirds of its surface, and the farmer asked him to test the crust's thickness with a probe from the walkway above.
options: decline the task as presented and suggest the probe test be done using a remotely operated device or with full PPE and a safety harness attached to a fixed anchor point
reach out carefully with the probe while keeping one hand on the railing
use a long stick instead of the probe to avoid getting close to the crust
lean over the railing and test the crust at the edge where it was obviously thicker
payload.explanation: Slurry lagoon crusts can collapse without warning and immersion in slurry is rapidly fatal — never lean over or approach a lagoon surface without fall protection and a safety system.

payload.snippet: She was helping the farm manager investigate why a herd of dairy cows had all produced very low yields that morning when she found that the automated feed dispenser had been dispensing double the normal urea supplement since the previous evening.
options: alert the farm manager immediately so a vet could assess the cows and the supplement be discontinued
turn off the supplement dispenser herself and observe the cows over the next few hours
dilute the remaining supplement in the hopper with plain feed before telling the farmer
complete the rest of her assigned tasks first and mention the issue at the end of the morning
payload.explanation: Urea toxicity in cattle progresses rapidly — immediate veterinary assessment alongside discontinuing the supplement is time-critical and must not be delayed by other work.

payload.snippet: He was on a farm experience day when he noticed that the temporary electric fencing around a paddock had been knocked over by cattle and a section of the energised wire was lying across a public footpath that walkers were approaching.
options: run to the nearest point where he could intercept the walkers, warn them to stop, and call the farmer simultaneously
drag the wire off the path using his rubber-soled boots
shout a warning from where he stood and wait for the walkers to hear him
call the farmer first and then run toward the walkers
payload.explanation: A live farm fence wire on a public path is an immediate public safety risk — running to intercept walkers and calling for help simultaneously addresses both the immediate and recovery actions in parallel.

payload.snippet: The farm was using a rented pesticide application drone in a top field, and she noticed the drone drifting toward the field boundary where a neighbour's honeybee hives were kept, despite the farmer having marked a 50-metre exclusion zone.
options: alert the operator and farmer immediately — the drone must be recalled before it crossed the exclusion boundary
watch to see whether the drone turned before reaching the boundary naturally
call out to the beehives' owner over the hedge to cover the hives quickly
photograph the drift to document it in case there was a complaint later
payload.explanation: Insecticide drift into bee hives causes colony collapse — a drone drifting toward the exclusion boundary must be recalled before it crosses, not after.

payload.snippet: She was taking water quality samples downstream from the farm when she found the water was bright orange, which it had not been during her previous visit a week earlier.
options: photograph the discolouration, note the GPS location, and call the environmental agency pollution hotline immediately
take an extra sample for testing and tell the farmer when the visit ended
add the sample to her normal water quality comparison without raising it separately
check whether it could be natural iron leaching before reporting it to anyone
payload.explanation: Sudden vivid water discolouration downstream of a farm is a pollution incident — the environment agency hotline exists for this purpose and must be called immediately, not after confirming the source.

payload.snippet: He was preparing to spray herbicide on a field boundary hedge when he checked the application certificate and realised it was issued in the name of the farm manager, not him, meaning he was not licenced to apply the product himself.
options: stop immediately and wait for the licenced farm manager to apply the product
apply the product under the farm manager's verbal supervision since she was nearby
apply the product since the certificate showed the farm was registered and he was farm staff
complete a quick online application for a temporary certificate before proceeding
payload.explanation: Pesticide application certificates are personal licences — applying any pesticide without a current valid certificate is illegal regardless of the farm's registration or verbal supervision.

payload.snippet: The class was on a farm visit when a sudden heavy hailstorm hit and the teacher asked her to lead the group quickly to the nearest barn for shelter, but the direct route crossed an open field with a visible electrical storm overhead.
options: route the group around the field edge, close to the hedgerow, rather than across the open centre
run straight across the open field since being wet was the bigger problem
spread the group out widely across the field to reduce the chance of a simultaneous lightning strike
wait under the large solitary oak tree at the field edge until the lightning passed
payload.explanation: Open field centres and isolated trees are the highest lightning risk points — moving along a hedgerow route reduces height and exposure compared to an open crossing or sheltering under a tree.
